title: Minimax Estimation of the Probability of Necessity with Many Sparse Covariate Cells
banked_reason: The package is therefore a substantive but specialized PN inference contribution rather than a general resolution of high-dimensional causal attribution.
gap_reasons: The identification formula and collision point-risk machinery are prior results, so the substantive increment is the PN-specific honest-inference and count-calibration package rather than a new general functional-estimation frontier.

The exact expected-length constant and two-way experiment comparison are proved only for the constructed one-dimensional correlated-sign hierarchy, while the corresponding full-class critical constant and equivalence remain open.

The absence of numerical solutions to the interval program, simulation evidence, or an application under the maintained growing-cell model limits the demonstrated practical significance and keeps the projected paper score below the strongest sharp-minimax benchmarks.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery established matched global PN risk and honest connected-interval length orders, a finite-sample corrected count interval, and a hierarchy-specific critical Poissonized-binomial calibration theorem. The all-n lower-bound witness and two external citations passed the final math review. The field target failed novelty review because the model is specialized and the full-class critical experiment and exact constant remain open; the achieved tier is subfield.
tldr: Under randomized binary treatment, known uniform \(d\)-cell covariates, and conditional independence of binary potential outcomes given the cell, PN is the identified ratio \(1-q/b\). On this growing-uniform half-randomized subclass, the paper establishes minimax squared risk \(\min\{1,n^{-1}+d/n^2\}\), the matching order for globally honest connected intervals, and a finite-sample observable collision-count interval. The root-\(n\) converse uses a bounded parametric pair that belongs to the model for every admissible \(n\), including \(n=1\). At \(d/n^2\to\kappa\), the correlated-sign critical hierarchy is uniformly comparable to its sufficient Poissonized-binomial experiment; an explicit semi-infinite program gives its local minimax expected-length constant, and an observable widened collision-count interval attains that constant with uniform-in-\(\zeta\) hierarchical coverage. This is not full-model experiment equivalence, and no exact full-class minimax constant is claimed. Generic expected-product rates remain prior machinery; the causal PN inference and count-calibration package is complete at the global order level.
gap: Tian and Wu identify PN under conditional independence and give fixed-model influence-function inference, while higher-order and discrete-causal papers establish generic bilinear and collision machinery. None of the inspected sources characterizes uniform PN estimation and globally honest connected intervals when the alphabet approaches \(n^2\), or calibrates inference through the observable four-mark collision process.
fill: The paper matches upper and lower decision-theoretic orders, controls the full observed-data likelihood under a correlated-sign mixture, derives a uniform marked-process approximation, and transfers exact conditional-binomial inversion to a finite-sample honest interval with actual-law expected-length control.
